document_title: 2024 AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guideline for Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Biomarker Interpretation
source: NIH National Library of Medicine / PubMed Central
authors: Whelton PK, Carey RM, Aronow WS, Casey DE Jr, Collins KJ, et al.
publisher: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology

sections.section_name: Fasting Blood Glucose & Metabolic Syndrome Thresholds
sections.content: A fasting blood glucose measurement equal to or exceeding 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) on two separate clinical assessments establishes the diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus and conveys a 2.4-fold elevated 10-year risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Patients presenting with impaired fasting glucose (100–125 mg/dL) require aggressive glycemic and lifestyle interventions to prevent microvascular and macrovascular target organ injury.

sections.section_name: Systolic Blood Pressure & Vascular Risk Stratification
sections.content: Stage 2 hypertension is defined as a persistent resting systolic blood pressure >= 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure >= 90 mmHg. Elevated systolic pressure directly accelerates arterial wall shear stress, left ventricular hypertrophic remodeling, and coronary endothelial dysfunction. Prompt initiation of dual antihypertensive combination therapy is strongly recommended for stage 2 hypertension with high predicted cardiovascular risk.

High-sensitivity cardiac Troponin-T (hs-cTnT) is the gold standard diagnostic biomarker for identifying acute and subacute myocardial injury. An hs-cTnT concentration exceeding 14 ng/L (0.014 ug/L), or an absolute delta change exceeding 7 ng/L over 3 hours, indicates active cardiomyocyte necrosis. Persistent minor elevations in asymptomatic individuals independently predict progressive congestive heart failure and long-term cardiac mortality.

document_title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T in Acute Coronary Syndromes and Ischemic Risk Stratification
source: Journal of the American College of Cardiology / PubMed
authors: Januzzi JL, McCarthy CP, Defilippi CR, et al.
publisher: Elsevier / American College of Cardiology Foundation

sections.content: Serial measurement of hs-cTnT provides high diagnostic sensitivity (98%) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). When evaluated alongside electrocardiographic signatures and multi-biomarker risk panels, elevated hs-cTnT (>14 ng/L) accurately differentiates acute ischemic events from chronic myocardial stress.
